author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: But what were we prior to the fall?
context_before: First called a son of God, you were told of the grand experiment in the statement, you shall die like men. Here is the plot for expansion and an ultimate birth.
context_after: I cannot describe that body, but I will use scripture in the hope that you will use your imagination, although I urge you not to come to any definite conclusions.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from God’S Wisest Creature (1968-01-01).

quote_original: The serpent has now become man!
context_before: his statement: “God knows you will not surely die, but your eyes will be opened and you will become like the gods, knowing good and evil.” (Genesis 3)
context_after: This serpent is described by Isaiah as the seraphim [sic]. Describing his vision, Isaiah said: “I beheld the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up. Above him were the seraphim.” In Hebrew, the word means glorious celestial being, fiery serpent, noble one, prince.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from God’S Wisest Creature (1968-01-01).
